planting.note: Root softwood cuttings in early summer or set out container-grown plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this vigorous Lemoine hybrid (Deutzia scabra x D. vilmorinae), raised in Nancy, France in 1909, forms a dense, upright, arching mound.

directions: Magnifica is an old French hybrid deutzia prized for the sheer density of its late-spring bloom, when arching branches become lined from tip to base with tight, rounded panicles of small, pure white, fully double flowers that give the whole shrub a frothy, snowball-like texture for about two weeks. The gray-green, hairy-backed leaves are typical of its Deutzia scabra parentage, and the shrub shares that species tendency toward an upright, somewhat coarse-textured habit that benefits from regular renewal. Because flowers form on the previous season's wood, prune immediately after bloom, cutting the oldest third of the canes to the ground each year to keep the planting dense and floriferous rather than tall and leggy. Give it full sun for the best flower set, though it tolerates light shade, and site it where its brief but showy bloom display can be appreciated from a distance along a border or screen.
